text:
Kim (Account): Hey team — prepping the Acero POC. Customer asked for a short 3-week sprint to validate latency, streaming UX, and auth model. Can we align scope and blockers?
Jordan (SE): +1. Proposed scope: 1) integration with our JS/Python SDKs, 2) streaming chat prototype (SSE or websockets), 3) quota/rate-limit behavior under load, 4) prompt evaluation set (10–20 cases).
Naveen (Customer): Confirming they want server-side API keys (rotated) and optional client-side short-lived tokens for browsers. Also need audit logs for requests.
Olivia (Security): For client tokens we recommend our short-lived token flow (STS) + mTLS for server-to-server in their prod env. We’ll need a security questionnaire answered (SOC2 questions).
Jordan (SE): For SDKs: Python snippet for server
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="sk-xxxx")
resp = c.chat.create(model="open-rl-13b", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}], stream=False)
```
For streaming use .stream parameter; we support SSE and websocket libs.
Lee (SRE): Quotas: default test quota we can grant is 200 requests/min and burst to 500 for short windows. For sustained throughput >500/min we need Dedicated trial. Also note concurrent streaming connections limited to 50 per org by default.
Kim (Account): Pricing question from the customer: they plan ~150k tokens/day in the POC. Which pricing tier applies for hosted usage and switching to Dedicated?
Jordan (SE): POC hosted -> usage pricing. At ~150k tokens/day we'd estimate ~$X/day (I dropped the exact $ in the doc). If they need predictable TCO we can recommend a short Dedicated eval (7–14 days) with reserved GPUs; I can pull numbers after exact prompt lengths.
Naveen (Customer): For success criteria: 1) p50 latency <250ms for short-turn queries, 2) streaming start within 500ms, 3) 80% of eval prompts return acceptable answers per their rubric, 4) logs + request IDs available in console. Is that doable in 3 weeks?
Jordan (SE): Looks reasonable. To hit p50 <250ms we'll recommend model variant "open-rl-13b-quant" + batching disabled for interactive flows. We'll enable KV caching for repeated prefixes.
Olivia (Security): Checklist items: A) confirm data retention period for logs, B) confirm encryption-in-transit and at-rest (we support both), C) share our SOC2 summary and customer-managed KMS options for Private.
Kim (Account): Timeline proposal: Week1: auth + SDK hookup + basic chat; Week2: streaming UX + telemetry; Week3: load test + eval prompts + wrap.
Lee (SRE): Load test plan: we'll run synthetic traffic up to 600 req/min for 30m windows to validate quotas and fallback. Add exponential retry guidance: initial_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=5s, max_retries=5. Use idempotency keys for non-streamed generate calls.
Jordan (SE): Integration notes to share with customer:
- Use Authorization: Bearer <key> header. For browser flows use short-lived token endpoint we provide.
- Telemetry: include X-Request-ID header and send user_id metadata so console groups traces.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for web demo (simpler), websockets for mobile if they need bi-directional.
Naveen (Customer): One blocker — their infra team requires the ability to rotate API keys via an API. Do we expose a key management API?
Olivia (Security): We can integrate with their KMS for Private, but hosted keys rotation via our console/API is supported; SEs can demo key rotation in the console and provide a small API snippet.
Jordan (SE): Action items:
- Jordan: prepare SDK quickstart + example streaming demo (due in 2 business days)
- Lee: provision test quota bump and schedule load window (ETA 48h)
- Olivia: send SOC2 excerpt + short-lived token flow doc (ETA 1 business day)
- Kim: confirm pricing estimate and commit terms with customer (ETA EOD)
- Naveen: gather 10 canonical prompts and the evaluation rubric by Tuesday
Kim (Account): Sounds good. I'll kick off a 30-min call with Acero tomorrow 10am PT to walk through these.
deploy-bot: scheduled reminder set for 2026-03-25 18:00 UTC — "POC kickoff: Acero 10am PT"
Naveen (Customer): Thanks all — I'll upload the eval prompts to the shared drive and invite Jordan.
Jordan (SE): I'll post the demo link and a minimal HTML + JS SSE example in the thread after I finish.
Kim (Account): Closing note — flag any enterprise blockers here (compliance, dedicated hardware needs, or legal), we'll surface to sales engineering leadership.
